title: Regional shard assignment and fail-safe routing policy for dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Dedicated capacity across multiple regions and zones need predictable throughput and a clear, auditable routing policy that preserves data residency constraints. Current behavior routes by simple priority lists and best-effort locality which leads to two issues: 1) unexpected cross-region serving during transient capacity shortages, and 2) opaque decisions during emergency failovers. Goal: Implement a regional shard-assignment + fail-safe routing policy that: (a) pins customer workloads to a regional shard with configurable zone dispersion, (b) provides a graded set of fail-safe routes (same-region spill, geo-fenced warm standby, controlled cross-region overflow) with explicit TTLs and audit logs, and (c) ties into autoscaling and throughput guarantees so SLA calculations remain accurate under failover. This ticket covers the policy definition, runtime routing extension, and a safe rollout plan for impacted Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL defined and documented in design doc with examples for single-region, multi-zone, and geo-redundant commitments
Runtime respects customer 'residency_lock' at region granularity and only permits cross-region overflow when policy and capacity thresholds are met
Routing decisions are emitted as structured tracing events and visible in Console per-request routing layer with region and reason codes
Canary rollout executed with three pilot customers, no SLA regression observed for 30 days, and automated rollback hooks in place
Runbook updated with escalation steps and required security/compliance checklist
proposed_solution: Introduce a two-layer routing model: a static shard assignment at allocation time and a dynamic fail-safe route graph. Shard assignment: when a customer purchase/commit is provisioned, we compute a primary regional shard and a zone dispersion vector (how many AZs to spread across). The shard is immutable for the commit lifetime unless a manual migration is requested. Fail-safe route graph: nodes are candidate fleets (primary-region pools, local warm standby, cross-region overflow pools). Edges have attributes: allowed (true/false), priority, max_latency_increase, TTL, and required_auth (to enforce compliance skips). The router evaluates capacity + latency + policy constraints to choose nodes. Integrations: autoscaler will expose projected free capacity per shard to the router; when projected capacity drops below a threshold, router will prefer warm standby before cross-region overflow. Add audit logs to Kinesis with structured reason codes (e.g., CAPACITY_PRESSURE, ZONE_EVICT, MAINTENANCE) and link traces to Console. The implementation will be feature-flagged by customer and by fleet to allow staged rollout.
tradeoffs: Immutable shard assignment simplifies billing and residency guarantees but makes live migrations harder; we'll provide an explicit migration path instead of transparent moves
Adding a warm-standby layer increases reserved overhead (cost) but reduces noisy cross-region fallbacks — tradeoff handled via product pricing tiers
More conservative default (no cross-region by default) reduces availability during extreme failures; product must opt-in for automatic cross-region overflow for critical customers
rollout_plan: Implement router extension + tracing hooks behind feature flags (ENG-620123-flag) — dev iteration: 2 weeks
Integration tests with autoscaler simulating capacity pressure and scheduled maintenance — run in staging (end-to-end)
Canary with 3 pilot customers in a single geobeat for two weeks, monitor SLOs and Console routing events
Broader opt-in release to Dedicated customers with admin toggle in Console, then default-on for new commitments after 2025-04-01
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: routing.cross_region_overflows.count (tagged by customer, reason)
SLO dashboards to show per-commit throughput vs committed throughput and post-failover delta
Alert: cross_region_overflows.count > 0 for >5 minutes for non-opted-in customers => paging
Audit log feed to security Kafka topic with retention and access controls; Console query to show last 7 days of routed events per commit
